Phase 7 isn’t delivered this turn. I hit the tool limit while still analyzing, so there are no new files yet. I did find why the current build is broken, and there’s a quick fix you can apply now.

Current master fails CI (commit 81a068c0)
The last run failed in testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug and produced no test reports, so it broke before tests ran. The cause is in the Phase 6 changes: they deleted <color name="indicator"> from values/colors.xml and values-night/colors.xml. Six drawables still use it, so resource linking fails:

drawable/sc_01_clock.xml
drawable/sc_02_compass.xml
drawable/sc_03_gps.xml
drawable/sc_04_level.xml
drawable/seek_bar.xml
drawable/text_field.xml
That color line was the only change to either file in Phase 6. You can restore both files exactly from the last green commit:

sh
git checkout 1f5c2396 -- app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml app/src/main/res/values-night/colors.xml
I checked every other layout, class and resource removed in Phase 6, and nothing else is still referenced. I can’t compile here because the sandbox can’t reach Google Maven, and I couldn’t download the CI log. I can’t rule out a Kotlin error hiding behind this one, so let CI confirm after the fix.

Phase 7 plan (sensor panels on Compose)
I’ve read the four panels, their layouts, the custom views and the helpers they use. The plan:

Shared pieces:
math/RotationPhysics.kt: a plain Kotlin version of the needle physics, with unit tests.
ui/compose/RotationState: animates a rotation only until it settles. The old PhysicalRotationImageView redrew every frame forever, which wastes battery.
sensors/: heading and gravity sensors that start and stop themselves with the screen.
PanelToolbar and InfoSection composables to replace the HTML text views.
Level: reads the gravity sensor about 50 times a second instead of as fast as possible. The tilt is mapped to the screen’s rotation, so landscape works properly.
Compass: you can still drag the dial and it returns afterwards. The bloom flowers stay, and the raw sensor readings update at most four times a second.
Direction: fixes a bug where the gimbal lock setting was ignored until you changed it.
Clock:
The hands are driven by the screen’s frame clock, so they stop updating when the app is in the background.
Sun and moon data are recalculated on a timer instead of on every GPS fix.
Polar locations, where sunrise or moonrise can be missing, no longer crash.
Custom-location changes take effect immediately.
The sun position diagram is redrawn with a Compose Canvas.
Deletions:
Views: PhysicalRotationImageView, SunPosition, VerticalTextView.
Layouts: all the level, compass, clock and direction layouts, including landscape, toolbars, info panels and generic_compass_rose.
Math: Quaternion, QuaternionMath, Euler, Vector3Utils, along with QuaternionTest and part of Vector3Test.
Utilities: DisplayRefreshRate, plus TimeFormatter.getTimeWithSeconds if nothing else uses it.
Kept: the existing menu, calibration and error dialogs are still opened from the new screens.
On the OpenStreetMap fallback
Noted for after Phase 9. You won’t need another API key: OSM’s public tiles are free under their usage policy, which asks you to identify your app and cache sensibly. osmdroid on the native Android side caches tiles and supports offline areas.

Send “continue” and I’ll write Phase 7 as a tar.gz of changed files, with the git rm list and an updated README.
